# Hydra-0: Action Flow for Generalist World Modeling and Control

> A generalist world model conditioned on action flow — robot actions represented
> as pixel motion. One model trains across embodiments, simulates them, evaluates
> policies, and drives a real robot.

Note on location: the llms.txt convention places this file at the origin root.
This copy is scoped to the Hydra-0 project page and describes only that page.

- Page: https://nvidia-isaac.github.io/video_to_data/hydra-0/

## Authors

Hongyu Li (NVIDIA; Brown University; Columbia University), Bowen Wen (NVIDIA),
Xinghao Zhu (NVIDIA), Yixuan Wang (NVIDIA), Yilun Du (NVIDIA; Harvard University),
Yunzhu Li (Columbia University), George Konidaris (Brown University),
Stan Birchfield (NVIDIA), Soha Pouya (NVIDIA), Chenran Li (NVIDIA), Yan Chang (NVIDIA).

## Summary

Hydra-0 is conditioned on **action flow**: robot actions represented as pixel motion
in the image plane. Because the interface is pixel-aligned rather than tied to
embodiment-specific joint or end-effector coordinates, one model learns from egocentric
human video, handheld UMI grippers, bimanual arms and single-arm robots at once. At
deployment it runs as a hybrid simulator — a physics engine moves the robot, the learned
video model predicts what the world does in response.

Headline results:

- 90.4% lower robot-motion error than the action-conditioned baseline
- 60.2% lower object-motion error than the same baseline
- Pearson r = 0.96 between replayed and reference success rates on RoboLab (300 episodes)
- 16.0x generation-only speedup after few-step distillation
- 2,202 hours of filtered multi-embodiment training video

The model also has an emergent **inverse mode**: given desired object flow transferred
from a human demonstration, it predicts compatible robot motion, and a trained action
head maps the resulting latent features to executable actions with no task-specific
expert robot demonstrations.

## Evaluation

Five held-out sets (XVLA-Soft-Fold, Deform360, DROID, MolmoAct2, ABC-130k), 100
validation clips each, against ATI, Wan-Move and Cosmos 2.5. Metrics: PSNR and SSIM
(image fidelity, higher better); object and gripper flow end-point error in pixels
(lower better); FID and FVD (distributional image/video distance, lower better); VLM
preference score (higher better). Object EPE is omitted for DROID, where object ground
truth is unavailable.

Complete per-dataset numbers for all seven models are in the "Full numerical results"
section of the page:
https://nvidia-isaac.github.io/video_to_data/hydra-0/#full-results

Media provenance for every clip on the page:
https://nvidia-isaac.github.io/video_to_data/hydra-0/media/MANIFEST.md
